analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing (November 2, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed mixed on Nov 2 (SPX +0.3%, NDX +0.5%, RTY +0.4%) as oil and bond yields fell on US/Iran deal optimism. Trump said there are no plans to strike Iran after the elections. Tech failed to hold its pre-market bid, with Memory and Semis reversing lower.
The ISM manufacturing production index rose 2.3 points to 59.0, the highest since November 2021. ISM new orders rose 0.2 points to 55.5 and the PMI new orders index eased to 53.1.

Price pressures stay elevated in the October manufacturing surveys. The PMI showed input cost inflation at its highest since May and output price inflation at its strongest since September 2022. ISM prices paid pulled back modestly but remained near its second-highest level since March 2022.

JPM Market Intel calls the ISM report a Goldilocks print: growth accelerating while inflationary impulses moderate but stay high. It says a Middle East resolution would be a tailwind and that Tech was oversold but has not yet had an all clear. It favors Cyclicals, SMid-Caps, Financials and Consumer plays as the broadening trade.

JPM midterm scenario odds: Blue Wave (Dem House/Dem Senate) 66%, Split Congress (Dem House/GOP Senate) 26%, Red Wave 7%, GOP House/Dem Senate 1%. Estimated SPX impact ranges from -25bp to +50bp in a Blue Wave up to +1% to +1.25% in a Red Wave.

SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, with an average gain of about 15%. Since 1990 the 6, 9 and 12 month returns after midterms have a 100% hit rate. Averages are +5.4% at 3 months, +11.4% at 6 months, +12.5% at 9 months and +14.7% at 12 months.
Early voting is up sharply, with 43mm votes cast as of Oct 30, about 10mm more than in 2022. Recent CNBC and Fox News polls show corruption replacing affordability as the top voting issue.

Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish. Its Positioning Intel data show that when NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it tends to rebound about 3% the following week. The effect is stronger when the decline happens on a Friday.

Market Intel argues an AI capex decline would not necessarily cause a recession. Its reasons are record household net worth and cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant driver of hiring. CRWV employs about 550 people. The main effect would be lower capex and possible hyperscaler layoffs.

The biggest non-AI risk is a Middle East re-escalation. A WSJ report describes considerable damage to US regional bases and depleted munitions, which JPM reads as limiting another wave of attacks and pointing to diplomacy. It says oil already prices that outcome, so upside to energy prices and bond yields is limited.

Monetization Menu (Nov 2): a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals, with Consumers and Financials working if the curve steepens. Look for Europe to catch a bid if a US/Iran deal progresses. In Jan-Feb, US Value gained 7.4%, SXXP 7.6% and UKX 9.7%.

TMT desk (Heavey): supportive flows in AMZN and GOOGL with MSFT as the source of funds. Names that can tap bond markets (GOOGL) are strong while Neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS) keep selling off. SMH reclaimed its 200-day average, with shorts pressed and elevated volumes. Security software is getting hit again, with CHKP the latest negative earnings data point and long selling continuing.

Fins desk (Barry): a 'buy-everything' tape in Financials, with heavily shorted subsectors rallying (M&A advisors, Payments, Alt Asset Managers). Volumes were -23% vs the 5-day average. The desk attributes moves to pod unwinds and quant de-grossing. RSP>QQQ is +13% since the selloff began on Oct 7.

Energy desk (Henrici): the energy team sees fair value at $94/bbl, so even at $104 about $10 of risk premium remains. Brent managed money net long is about 250mm barrels, about 20% above the post-2020 average. CTA positioning in Brent and WTI is firmly long, and the commodity team screens Brent about 5 out of 10.

Healthcare desk (Bukzin): last week's moves felt machine-driven and systematic. There was generalist rotation into pharma (MRK), dedicated funds adding to biotech longs, a preference to own Medicaid-exposed managed care (CNC), and mostly hedge fund driven activity in Med tech.

Consumer desk (Barton) on YUM ahead of its Nov 3 release: positioning is mixed-to-positive. Street expects +2% Q4 Taco Bell comps and +5% for FY27. Buy-side expectations are below the street at a Taco Bell bogey of down 4-5% (street -2.4%), with KFC in line at +2%.

Key week ahead: JOLTS and Factory Orders on Nov 3 with the midterm election, ISM Services on Nov 4, NFP on Nov 6, BoE rate decision on Nov 5, CPI on Nov 10, and a Fed meeting on Dec 9. A US government funding deadline falls on Dec 11.

risk_factors: Middle East re-escalation is the biggest non-AI risk, though JPM sees limited upside for oil, yields and downside for equities.
Weekend AI headlines were negative on capital raising (CNBC), circular financing (WSJ) and legal matters (CNBC).
The market could use added liquidity under a Blue Wave to de-gross within the AI theme.
Investigation risk for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech (WSJ).
Elevated deficit spending under a Red Wave could push longer-dated bond yields higher.
Tariffs, energy and commodity prices, and Middle East disruptions weigh on manufacturing, and supply chains remain under stress.
A decline in AI capex could affect GDP growth and hyperscaler layoffs.
vol_and_positioning: NDX within about 6% of its all-time high with a 3.5%+ decline has historically rebounded about 3% the following week, more so when the decline occurs on a Friday.
Brent managed money net long is about 250mm barrels, up about 150mm barrels from the June low and about 20% above the post-2020 average.

CTA positioning in Brent and WTI is firmly long on the delta one screen, up from moderately long in late September. The commodity team screens Brent about 5 out of 10, and it never exceeded 8 in 2026.
Shorts are being pressed in semis while volumes are elevated, and shorts are engaging CPU-linked plays after the INTC drop last week.
The Fins desk sees heavily shorted subsectors rallying, which it ties to hedge fund unwinds. It says pod unwinds and quant de-grossing are driving moves, with desk volumes -23% vs the 5-day average.
MSFT is the general source of funds for AMZN and GOOGL buying.
geopolitical: US/Iran deal optimism lifted markets, and Trump told reporters there are no plans to strike Iran after the elections.
Iran's Khamenei gave the government powers to hold talks on the war (BBG headline).
A WSJ report describes considerable damage to US regional bases from Iran and depleted US munitions.
Democrats could pull funding or force a troop removal from the Iran conflict after the new Congress is seated in January, since US forces are engaged beyond 90 days without Congressional approval.
US pushes to restore Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine (WSJ headline). US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Under a Blue Wave, investors bullish on AI can buy any dip, since Trump has said he will not sign bills limiting AI expansion and Democrats cannot achieve a veto-proof majority.
tension_points.bear_case: Many fear an AI sell-off on assumed higher regulation, and the market could use added liquidity to de-gross within the AI theme.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Blue Wave outcome that produces investigations of MegaCap Tech leaders tied to Trump donations.

tension_points.bull_case: Consumer balance sheets and corporate margins are strong, and AI is not a significant driver of hiring, so a capex decline does not drive a recession.
tension_points.bear_case: A capex decline could hit GDP growth metrics and cause hyperscaler layoffs, with a negative wealth effect from a bear market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Corporate margins would need to compress before mass layoffs begin.

tension_points.bull_case: US/Iran deal optimism has driven oil and yields lower, with a Middle East resolution a boon for markets.
tension_points.bear_case: Re-escalation is the biggest non-AI risk, although JPM says oil already prices this and upside is limited.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another series of attacks on Iran after the elections.
